investing: A Utah mineral investment should be traced from the recorded interest to the paid decimal before a yield or multiple is trusted. The file identifies the county, legal description, estate type, ownership fraction, lease royalty, unit participation, deductions, taxes, producing wells, operator, statement months, and title assumptions still open.
Separate the Uinta or Paradox Case

Nearby wells, units, permits, operator activity, and a basin label can add context without proving future development. Base, downside, and upside cases need the same ownership fraction and paid decimal.

For Uinta production, realized pricing, heating, gathering, trucking or rail, refinery access, and other deductions should appear as separate assumptions rather than disappear inside a generic price deck.

Every material number should keep its source and date. The record should state the holding period, liquidity limits, title expense, tax questions, and the event that would invalidate the original case.
Reconcile the Model to the Utah Conveyance

{name} still depends on the estate described in the recorded chain. The investment file should identify the legal description, acquired fraction, any depth or formation limit, present payor, suspense status, and unresolved ownership issue. That reconciliation prevents a clean-looking model from assuming acreage or rights the seller cannot convey.
Stress the Paid Decimal Against Actual Statements

The review should compare several statement months rather than treating one check as normal. Oil, gas, and natural-gas-liquids volumes, price, taxes, deductions, prior-period adjustments, downtime, and suspense releases can move independently. For nonproducing acreage, the file states clearly that permits, nearby wells, or operator activity are development evidence rather than current cash flow.
Write the Downside Case Before the Upside Case

A disciplined Utah mineral model tests lower volumes, weaker realized pricing, longer downtime, higher heat-and-haul costs, unresolved title expense, operator concentration, and delayed development before giving weight to upside permits or nearby activity. The downside case should show which assumption changes the value conclusion first.
Set a Review Date for Every Material Assumption

Production, operator activity, unit records, statement deductions, title status, and market liquidity can change on different schedules. The decision file assigns a source date and a future review date to each material assumption so the investment case can be updated without rebuilding the record from memory.
exchange-1031: Potential exchange treatment should be discussed with a qualified intermediary and independent tax counsel before a sale closes or proceeds are received. The file identifies the selling entity, Utah property, expected proceeds, closing date, deadlines, and proposed replacement property.
Keep Utah Curative Work and Federal Timing Distinct

Deed work, probate, heirship, trusts, corrective instruments, and payor records can move on a different schedule from exchange deadlines. Each open item needs a responsible professional and written status.

The sale agreement, deed, legal description, retained-rights language, settlement statement, intermediary instructions, and replacement identification should not quietly change acreage, estate, formation, depth, county, or ownership fraction.

The completed file should retain the agreement, recorded deed, exact legal description, settlement statement, intermediary instructions, identification notices, replacement documents, title correspondence, and recording information.
Tie the Exchange File to the Conveyed Utah Interest

{name} should not float free of the tract record. The owner file should show the exact county, legal description, estate type, ownership fraction, retained rights, deed form, settlement amount, and recording reference beside the intermediary timeline.

The qualified intermediary handles exchange funds and required notices; independent tax counsel evaluates eligibility and reporting; title counsel addresses deed, entity, probate, trust, and curative questions; the closing team confirms the tract, estate, fraction, consideration, and recording package. A dated issue list reduces the risk that proceeds are received by the wrong party or an incomplete property description reaches a required notice.
Reconcile Identification Language to the Replacement Record

A replacement-property identification should be reviewed against the actual property records available at the time. Names, legal descriptions, county references, entity ownership, percentage interests, and stated alternatives need consistent language across the notice, purchase documents, title file, and closing instructions.
Archive the Completed Exchange and Utah Title Files Together

The final owner copy should retain intermediary instructions, dated identification notices, settlement statements, recorded conveyances, title correspondence, funding records, replacement-property documents, professional advice, and the Utah mineral file. Keeping both records together makes later reporting and ownership questions easier to answer.
